question: A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of pain and weakness in her right forearm and hand for several months. Two years ago, she sustained a fracture of her ulnar shaft with dislocation of the radial head that was treated surgically. Physical examination shows mild tenderness a few centimeters distal to the lateral epicondyle. She has marked weakness when attempting to extend her right middle finger. There is radial deviation on extension of the wrist. Sensation is not impaired. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Forearm pain and weakness" -> "Weakness in finger extension" -> "Radial deviation on wrist extension" -> "Posterior interosseous nerve involvement" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Forearm pain and weakness" -> "Weakness in finger extension" -> "No sensory impairment" -> "Posterior interosseous nerve involvement" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Forearm pain and weakness" -> "History of ulnar shaft fracture" -> "Surgical treatment" -> "Possible nerve injury" -> "Posterior interosseous nerve involvement" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Forearm pain and weakness" -> "Tenderness distal to lateral epicondyle" -> "Weakness in finger extension" -> "Posterior interosseous nerve involvement" -> 90%
enhanced_information: The patient's symptoms of forearm pain, weakness in finger extension, and radial deviation on wrist extension, without sensory impairment, align with posterior interosseous nerve involvement. This nerve, a branch of the radial nerve, is responsible for motor innervation to the extensor muscles of the forearm, which explains the weakness in finger extension and radial deviation. The tenderness distal to the lateral epicondyle suggests possible compression or injury to this nerve, which is consistent with the history of surgical treatment for an ulnar shaft fracture. The retrieved evidence paths broadly associate forearm pain and asthenia with nerve involvement, supporting the conclusion that the posterior interosseous nerve is affected. Therefore, the posterior interosseous nerve is the most likely affected nerve in this patient.
analysis: The patient's symptoms include pain and weakness in the right forearm and hand, specifically marked weakness in extending the right middle finger and radial deviation on wrist extension. These symptoms, along with the absence of sensory impairment, suggest an issue with the motor function of the extensor muscles of the forearm. The posterior interosseous nerve, a branch of the radial nerve, is responsible for innervating these muscles. The tenderness distal to the lateral epicondyle aligns with the anatomical course of the posterior interosseous nerve, which can be compressed or injured in this area, especially following surgical treatment for an ulnar shaft fracture. The lack of sensory impairment further supports the involvement of the posterior interosseous nerve, as it primarily affects motor function. Therefore, the most likely affected nerve in this patient is the posterior interosseous nerve.
